articleHeadline: Doctors flag alarming rise in antibiotic-resistant UTI cases
articleSummary: Hyderabad reports rising highly antibiotic-resistant urinary tract infections (UTIs) in government and private hospitals, now about three to four cases weekly vs roughly one per month earlier. Underlying causes like urinary stones, blockages, prostate issues, incomplete bladder emptying, and catheter use can drive recurrence.

articleHeadline: Woman's Hallucinations And Headaches Hid A Terrifying Diagnosis: Doctors Discovered A Parasite In Her Brain
articleSummary: In the Philippines, a 52-year-old woman with four months of headaches and visual hallucinations, plus speech difficulties, was diagnosed with neurocysticercosis. MRI showed multiple brain cysts, some containing a bright spot—the scolex of Taenia solium larva. EEG revealed abnormal activity suggesting seizures. She received antiparasitic therapy and seizure treatment; within a month her symptoms resolved and follow-up scans showed cysts shrinking and the bright scolex spots disappearing. Neurocysticercosis arises when T. solium eggs are ingested, traveling to the brain via the bloodstream after fecal contamination of food, water, or surfaces. Eggs can cause disease without pork consumption; possible exposure in evacuation centers with poor sanitation over the prior year. Symptoms may emerge months to years after infection and include headaches, seizures, confusion, or language difficulties. Prevention emphasizes hygiene, safe water and food, and treating intestinal tapeworms.
